description: The Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) is the European Union's planned multimodal network of railways, inland waterways, short sea shipping routes and roads linking urban nodes, maritime and inland ports, airports and terminals, set out in Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 in three layers: the core network (to be completed by 2030), the extended core network (2040) and the comprehensive network (2050), with nine European Transport Corridors. The European Commission's DG MOVE maintains it in TENtec, its information system for TEN-T policy, which publishes public interactive map viewers and ArcGIS map services. On 26 September 2026 the public TENT_Regulation_2024 service held layers for rail-road terminals (256), ports (616), airports (423), urban nodes and capitals, roads, freight railways (1,994 core sections) and passenger railways by network layer, and inland waterways (893), with attributes such as member state, corridor, core or comprehensive status and length. Further public services cover corridors, alternative fuels infrastructure, border crossing points, C-ITS stations, projects and military mobility. Access is free and open without login; the services support map, query and data requests returning JSON and GeoJSON, and Commission content is licensed CC BY 4.0. Caveats: this is a policy network, so sections include planned links, and the detailed compliance and project data in TENtec are restricted to registered users. The layers give the network topology for network flow, cross-border freight and resilience studies of European corridors, and complement the Eurostat transport statistics and the ERA register of railway infrastructure catalogued here.
